guideTitle: 6 Best Ultrasonic Cleaners for Coins in 2026
metaDescription: Six ultrasonic cleaners compared on frequency, tank size and cycles for everyday coins and small metal pieces, with clear advice on collectible coins.
introParagraphs: Pocket change, souvenir tokens and craft coins pick up skin oil, grease and grime that a brush struggles to reach in the rims and lettering. An ultrasonic cleaner can lift that film without scrubbing, which is a welcome change when small items and fine detail work have become tiring on the hands. The catch is that coins are not like rings or eyeglasses, and the cleaner you choose matters less than knowing which coins to leave alone.

That caution comes first. Collectors and grading services generally treat cleaning as damage, because it can strip toning and change the surface, so a coin with any possible collector value should never go in a machine. This guide is for everyday and circulated coins, tokens, craft pieces and similar small metal items, where the goal is simply a cleaner object.

We evaluated six home-sized models based on product specs and buyer feedback, focusing on frequency, tank capacity, cycle options and what each maker says about limits. Use the picks, criteria and decision tables below to match a machine to your habits.

products.name: Magnasonic 20oz Stainless Steel Ultrasonic Cleaner
products.description:
The Magnasonic is a straightforward 42,000 Hz tub with a 20 oz (600 ml) stainless steel tank, a digital timer and five cleaning cycles that run from quick to deep. Its listing names coins among the items it handles, alongside jewelry, glasses, watches and tools. A basket comes in the box, so coins stay off the tank floor and lift out in one go.

The tradeoff is that there is no heater, and the listing states plainly that it does not remove tarnish. Tarnish and toning on a coin are changes to the metal surface, so a cycle will lift dirt and grease but will not turn a dark coin bright. For anyone worried about over-cleaning, that limit is a safety feature rather than a flaw.

Day to day you fill it with tap water to the line, set the basket in and pick a cycle. The 600 ml tank holds a good handful of coins spread out, where the 350 ml OSLTWI fits noticeably fewer at once. The 800 ml VisiClean has more room and a second transducer, but the Magnasonic keeps the simplest controls of the three.
products.bestFor: Households that want one dependable machine for everyday coins, jewelry and glasses.
pros: Five preset cycles remove the guesswork about how long to run coins
The 42,000 Hz output is gentler than a 40 kHz workshop machine
The 600 ml stainless tank holds a handful of coins spread in the basket
The included basket keeps coins off the tank floor and easy to lift out
cons: No heater, so greasy coins rely on time and a drop of mild detergent
The listing says it will not remove tarnish or toning from metal
The 600 ml tank is too small for a large bulk lot of coins at once

products.name: VisiClean 800 ml Dual Transducer Ultrasonic Cleaner
products.description:
The VisiClean pairs 42,000 Hz output with two transducers that the listing says double the cleaning power, inside an 800 ml (27 oz) stainless steel tank. A built-in cooling fan, touch controls and five presets round out the package, and coins are named on its list of suitable items. It runs from standard 110V power.

The maker gives clear limits, which is useful guidance: no hot water, and no run longer than 30 minutes. For coins that suits you well, because warm water and long soaks are exactly what you want to avoid with metal that can darken or pit. The unit is bulkier than a drawer-sized jewelry tub, so it wants a permanent spot on a shelf.

The lid is removable and non-hinged and the power cord detaches, which makes filling, draining and wiping the tank easier than on fixed-cord designs. At 800 ml it has room for a bigger batch of pocket change than the 600 ml Magnasonic. Against the 650 ml Blazeavian it adds a second transducer and a fan, at the cost of a larger footprint.
products.bestFor: People cleaning a big jar of pocket change or a mix of coins, glasses and dentures.
pros: Dual transducers add cleaning power while staying at a gentle 42,000 Hz
The 800 ml tank is the roomiest of the home-sized machines in this guide
A removable lid and detachable cord make filling and storing easier
The built-in cooling fan helps the unit cope with longer cleaning cycles
cons: The maker advises no hot water, so there is no warm-clean option
It should not run beyond 30 minutes, so plan short cycles for coins
Larger than the compact tubs, so it needs a permanent shelf spot

products.name: onlikin 35W 45kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 20oz
products.description:
The onlikin runs at 45 kHz with 35W of power and lets you choose from three power levels, which is the most control in this group over how hard the bubbles work. Five timers (90, 180, 300, 420 and 480 seconds) appear on a digital display with touch control. The 20 oz tank is 304 stainless steel, and the listing names coins among the items it suits.

Power levels matter for coins because you can start low and stop early on anything you are unsure about. The 480 second cycle also triggers a built-in degassing process, according to the listing, which is aimed at retainers but helps any load. The tradeoff is that 35W is modest, so it is a grime-lifting machine rather than one for heavy, baked-on soil.

The listing claims operation below 38 dB, the lowest noise figure in this lineup. Setup is fill, choose power, choose time. Compared with the Magnasonic's five fixed cycles at 42,000 Hz, the onlikin adds the power selector, and against the LifeBasis at 45 kHz it matches the frequency but has no cooling fan.
products.bestFor: Careful cleaners who want to start gently and step power up only when needed.
pros: Three selectable power levels let you start gentle on unfamiliar coins
Five timers from 90 to 480 seconds keep each cycle short and controlled
The listing claims operation under 38 dB for quiet use at a kitchen table
The 304 stainless tank resists corrosion and wear from regular use
cons: At 35W it is a light-duty machine for heavy grease or baked-on residue
Three power levels plus five timers means a few more steps per cycle
No cooling fan is listed, so space out longer cycles to avoid warming

products.name: Blazeavian 49kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 650 ml
products.description:
The Blazeavian runs at 49 kHz, the highest frequency in this guide, which produces the smallest bubbles and the gentlest clean. Its 650 ml (22 oz) tank is 304 stainless steel and the case measures 8.86 by 3.93 by 2.95 inches. Three modes of 3, 6 and 12 minutes cover a light refresh through an intensive clean.

The listing does not name coins, so suitability for coins is inferred from its general metal-cleaning ability rather than a stated use. There is also no power selector, so you get three fixed run times and nothing finer. That makes it a good fit for people who want gentle and simple, and a poor fit for anyone who wants to tune every cycle.

Four silicone pads under the base reduce vibration and noise and keep the unit steady on a counter. A 12-month warranty is listed. Next to the 350 ml OSLTWI at 48 kHz it offers nearly the same gentleness with almost twice the tank, while the 800 ml VisiClean has more room and a second transducer at 42,000 Hz.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants the gentlest frequency in a mid-size tank with only three simple modes.
pros: At 49 kHz it is the gentlest frequency in this lineup for small metal
Three fixed modes of 3, 6 and 12 minutes keep cycles short and simple
Four silicone pads cut vibration and keep the unit steady on a counter
The 650 ml tank is almost double the size of the OSLTWI at 350 ml
cons: Coins are not named in the listing, so suitability is inferred only
No power selector, so you cannot dial the cleaning strength down further
The 12 minute deep mode is the longest, so watch it with delicate items

products.name: LifeBasis CDS-100 Ultrasonic Cleaner, 600 ml
products.description:
The LifeBasis CDS-100 runs at 45 kHz in a 600 ml (20 oz) SUS 304 stainless tank, with five cycles of 90, 180, 300, 480 and 600 seconds on a digital display. Every run begins with a 20-second degassing step that clears trapped air from the water, so the energy goes into your coins instead of into bubbles. A built-in cooling fan and overheating protection are listed, along with automatic shut-off.

The automatic degas is the standout, since you do not have to remember a separate mode. The tradeoff is that there are no power levels, so the only way to be gentle is to choose a short cycle. The listing does not name coins specifically, though it covers jewelry, utensils, watches and other metal items.

The cord is removable, which makes swapping water and storing it easy. It holds the same 600 ml as the Magnasonic, but it runs at 45 kHz instead of 42,000 Hz and adds the degas step and a fan. Against the onlikin at 35W it gives up the power selector in return for the automatic degas.
products.bestFor: People who want better results from plain water without managing a degas mode.
pros: A 20-second degas starts every cycle so energy reaches the coins
Five cycles from 90 to 600 seconds cover light and heavy cleaning
A cooling fan and overheat protection help it cope with longer runs
The removable power cord makes changing water and storing it simple
cons: No power selector, so gentleness depends only on cycle length
Coins are not named in the listing, only general metal items
The 600 second top cycle is long, so use it only on hardy pieces

products.name: OSLTWI 48kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 350 ml
products.description:
The OSLTWI runs at 48 kHz in a 350 ml 304 stainless steel tank, and the whole unit weighs only 0.57 kg. A single one-touch selector switches between two cleaning modes, so there is almost nothing to learn. The high frequency makes it a gentle option for small metal pieces and light daily grime.

The small tank is the honest tradeoff. A few coins fit spread out, but a jar of change needs several rounds, and with only two modes you have less control than the five-cycle machines. The listing leans heavily on marketing claims, so we focused on the plain specs of frequency, tank, weight and mode count.

Because it is light and compact it can live in a drawer and come out for a weekly clean. Fill with water, press the button and rinse the items afterward. Compared with the 600 ml Magnasonic it holds far less, and next to the 650 ml Blazeavian at 49 kHz it offers nearly the same frequency in a smaller, lighter body.
products.bestFor: Small households cleaning a few coins or tokens at a time who value a simple tub.
pros: At 48 kHz it is a gentle option for small metal pieces and tokens
Weighs only 0.57 kg, so it stores easily in a drawer between uses
A one-touch selector keeps operation simple for any household member
The 304 stainless tank resists wear, scratches and corrosion
cons: The 350 ml tank means several rounds to clean a larger jar of change
Only two cleaning modes, so less control than the five-cycle models
No heater and no fine timer control to tune the length of each cycle

buyingCriteria.criterion: Which coins are safe to clean
buyingCriteria.explanation: This is the first decision, and it has nothing to do with the machine. Collectors generally treat cleaning as damage, because it can remove toning and change the surface, so any coin that might have collector value should stay out of every cleaner. Use ultrasonic cleaning only on circulated change, tokens, craft pieces and similar everyday metal. If you are unsure whether a coin matters, set it aside and ask a dealer before you wash it. None of the six picks here, from the 200 to 800 ml home tubs, changes that rule.

Higher frequency makes smaller bubbles and a gentler clean, which is the safer direction for small metal pieces. The Blazeavian runs at 49 kHz, the OSLTWI at 48 kHz, the onlikin and LifeBasis at 45 kHz, and the Magnasonic and VisiClean at 42,000 Hz. Aim for 42 kHz or higher for coins, and prefer a unit with short cycles. The onlikin goes one step further with three selectable power levels at 35W, which lets you start low and step up only if needed.

Coins should sit in a basket and be spread out rather than piled, so the tank limits how many you can do per cycle. A 350 ml tank like the OSLTWI handles a few coins at a time, 600 to 650 ml in the Magnasonic, LifeBasis and Blazeavian handles a handful, and the VisiClean at 800 ml is the largest here. Piling coins means they contact each other while the bath is running, which defeats the point. Check that a basket is included, as it is with the Magnasonic.

Short cycles are the safe default for metal you cannot replace. The VisiClean maker says no hot water and no run beyond 30 minutes, while the Blazeavian tops out at a 12 minute mode and the LifeBasis at 600 seconds. Start with the shortest cycle, check the coins, and repeat only if needed. None of these six picks has a heater, which is a plus here, because warm solution is more aggressive on metal.

Ultrasonic cleaning removes loose dirt, skin oil and grease, but it does not reverse chemical change. The Magnasonic listing says outright that it does not remove tarnish, and the same is true of every machine here. A dark coin will come out cleaner, not shiny, and chasing a bright finish by running longer cycles is how people overdo it. Set the expectation first: the goal is a clean coin, not a new one.

A cleaner you enjoy using gets used. The onlikin lists operation below 38 dB, the Blazeavian has four silicone pads to reduce vibration, and the OSLTWI at 0.57 kg is the easiest to put away. The VisiClean is the roomiest at 800 ml but needs a permanent shelf, though its detachable cord and removable lid help with storage. Think about where you will fill and drain it, since water handling is the main chore.

howWeEvaluated.title: Gentleness and control
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated frequency, power and cycle options for each machine. The Blazeavian leads on gentleness at 49 kHz, the onlikin leads on control with three power levels at 35W, and the Magnasonic and VisiClean sit at 42,000 Hz. These are manufacturer figures, so we treated them as relative rather than exact.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tank size and basket
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how many coins each tank can reasonably hold when spread out. The VisiClean holds 800 ml, the Blazeavian 650 ml, the Magnasonic and LifeBasis 600 ml, and the OSLTWI 350 ml. Machines with an included basket, like the Magnasonic, earned extra credit for keeping items off the tank floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cycle options and limits
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared presets, fixed modes and any maker limits on run time or water temperature. The Magnasonic and VisiClean offer five presets, the LifeBasis five timed cycles with automatic degas, the Blazeavian three modes, and the OSLTWI two. The VisiClean's no-hot-water and 30 minute guidance counted in its favor as clear instruction.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for coins and metal
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each listing names coins or general metal items, and gave weight to guidance about delicate use. The Magnasonic, VisiClean and onlikin name coins directly, while the Blazeavian, LifeBasis and OSLTWI cover general small metal. We did not treat any listing as permission to clean collectible coins.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered noise claims, weight, cords, lids and warranty terms. The onlikin lists under 38 dB, the OSLTWI is the lightest at 0.57 kg, the VisiClean has a detachable cord and removable lid, and the Blazeavian lists a 12-month warranty. We did not rank on price, only on what each model offers within its size class.

faq.q: Should I clean valuable or collectible coins in an ultrasonic cleaner?
faq.a: No. Collectors and grading services generally treat cleaning as damage, because it can strip toning and alter the surface, and that can lower a coin's value. If a coin might be old, scarce or silver, leave it alone and ask a dealer. These machines are for everyday change, tokens and craft pieces.

faq.q: Which ultrasonic cleaner is best for most people cleaning coins?
faq.a: For most households the Magnasonic is the safest all-round pick, with its 42,000 Hz output, 600 ml tank, included basket and five cycles. If you clean large batches, the 800 ml VisiClean has more room and dual transducers. If you want to control strength, the onlikin offers three power levels at 35W.

faq.q: Will an ultrasonic cleaner make dark coins shiny again?
faq.a: Usually not. Ultrasonic cleaning removes dirt, skin oil and grease, but toning and tarnish are chemical changes to the metal surface. The Magnasonic listing says directly that it does not remove tarnish. Expect a cleaner coin, and avoid running long cycles in search of a shine.

faq.q: Is a higher frequency better for coins?
faq.a: Higher frequency is gentler rather than stronger. The Blazeavian at 49 kHz and the OSLTWI at 48 kHz make smaller bubbles than the 42,000 Hz Magnasonic and VisiClean. For small metal pieces that gentleness is a safe direction, though power and tank design also affect results.

faq.q: Can I use hot water or a cleaning solution?
faq.a: Check your model's guidance first. The VisiClean maker advises against hot water and against running beyond 30 minutes, and none of the six picks has a heater. Plain tap water handles most grime, and a drop of mild detergent can help with oily film, if the manual allows it.

faq.q: How do I keep an ultrasonic cleaner working for years?
faq.a: Empty and dry the tank after every session and never run it without liquid. Keep cycles to the maker's limits, because small units warm up on long runs. The VisiClean's detachable cord and removable lid make cleaning easy, and a basket keeps coins off the tank floor. Wipe the control panel with a damp cloth rather than spraying it.

faq.q: How should I load coins into the basket?
faq.a: Spread them out in a single layer where you can, rather than piling them, so every surface faces the bath. Fill the tank to the line before you switch on, and never run it empty. In a 350 ml OSLTWI that means a few coins per cycle, while the 800 ml VisiClean can take a larger spread.
